evidence.description: Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) activity involves multiple systems or sources generating coordinated network traffic against a targeted service or resource.
indicators: High-volume traffic originating from multiple sources
Coordinated traffic from many systems toward the same target
Large increase in packet or flow rates
Multiple source addresses targeting one service or resource
Network bandwidth exhaustion caused by aggregated traffic
Reduced availability or functionality of the targeted resource
detection_guidance: Identify whether abnormal traffic originates from multiple source systems
Measure aggregated packet and flow rates toward the target
Identify many source addresses communicating with the same destination or service
Look for coordinated traffic patterns across distributed sources
Compare the aggregated traffic against the normal network baseline
mitigation_guidance: Use upstream filtering when attack volume exceeds local network capacity

evidence.description: Brute Force is a credential-access technique involving repeated attempts to obtain valid credentials.
indicators: Repeated authentication failures
High volume of failed login attempts
Repeated attempts against accounts or services
Authentication failures from suspicious sources
Multiple accounts targeted within a short time period
Failed authentication attempts followed by successful login
detection_guidance: Monitor authentication failures and identify unusually high volumes
Correlate authentication failures by source, account, host, and time
Look for repeated failures followed by successful authentication
Identify authentication attempts distributed across multiple accounts
Monitor externally exposed authentication services
mitigation_guidance: Implement appropriate account-use and lockout policies
Reset accounts associated with known compromised credentials
Apply conditional access policies where appropriate

evidence.description: Network Service Discovery is a reconnaissance technique in which adversaries attempt to identify services and protocols running on systems accessible through a network.
indicators: Connections to multiple destination ports
Connections to multiple hosts
Repeated connection attempts
Probing of network services
Unusual network service discovery activity
detection_guidance: Monitor connections to multiple ports or hosts
Identify unusual patterns of network service probing
Correlate repeated connection attempts from the same source
Investigate scanning activity against exposed systems
mitigation_guidance: Use network monitoring and filtering controls

evidence.description: Denial of Service (DoS) activity attempts to make a system or service unavailable by overwhelming or exhausting its resources.
indicators: Abnormally high traffic or request volume targeting a service
Repeated requests directed at a specific host or service
Unusual packet or flow rates associated with the target
Resource exhaustion affecting the targeted service
Service performance degradation or unavailability
Traffic pattern concentrated on a particular target
detection_guidance: Examine traffic volume and request rates targeting the affected service
Determine whether activity is concentrated on a specific host or service
Compare the observed traffic against the normal service baseline
Investigate repeated requests or connections targeting the same resource
Examine the source distribution to distinguish concentrated DoS activity from distributed DDoS activity

evidence.description: Botnet activity can involve compromised systems communicating with external infrastructure under adversary control.
indicators: Repeated communication with suspicious external systems
Unusual outbound network connections
Persistent communication patterns
Similar communication behavior across multiple hosts
Unexpected connections to external infrastructure
Coordinated network activity from compromised systems
detection_guidance: Identify unusual outbound communication patterns
Monitor repeated connections to suspicious external systems
Compare communication behavior across multiple hosts
Investigate persistent or coordinated external communication
Correlate network flows with endpoint activity where available
mitigation_guidance: Remove malware or the underlying compromise
Monitor systems for recurring suspicious communication

evidence.description: Web attacks target web applications through malicious requests or input intended to exploit application weaknesses, obtain unauthorized access, or affect application behavior.

attack_categories.name: SQL Injection
attack_categories.description: Malicious input is used to interfere with SQL queries executed by an application.

attack_categories.name: Cross-Site Scripting
attack_categories.description: Malicious script content is injected into web application content and may execute in a user's browser.

attack_categories.name: Web Application Brute Force
attack_categories.description: Repeated authentication or access attempts target web application accounts or protected resources.

indicators: Unusual HTTP requests
Suspicious request parameters
Repeated requests targeting application endpoints
SQL-related injection patterns
Unexpected script content in input
Repeated authentication attempts against web applications
detection_guidance: Monitor HTTP request patterns
Inspect suspicious request parameters
Monitor repeated requests to sensitive endpoints
Correlate web requests with application and authentication logs
Look for abnormal input patterns associated with injection attacks
mitigation_guidance: Use parameterized queries for database access
Keep web applications and dependencies patched
Use appropriate web application security controls

evidence.description: Benign represents network traffic that is not labeled as one of the attack categories represented in the CIC-IDS2017 dataset.
indicators: Traffic does not match the attack labels in the dataset
No significant attack pattern identified by the trained classifier
investigation_guidance: Verify that the observed traffic is consistent with expected behavior
Consider additional contextual information when activity appears unusual
Review related network and system events when necessary

evidence.description: Adversaries may exploit vulnerabilities in remote services to gain unauthorized access to systems and move into an environment.
indicators: Unexpected remote service connections
Unusual internal network activity
Connections from suspicious or compromised hosts
Exploitation of exposed services
Unexpected lateral movement
detection_guidance: Investigate unusual remote service connections
Review network traffic between internal hosts
Identify the source and destination systems involved
Check authentication and system logs for suspicious activity
Investigate signs of exploitation or lateral movement
mitigation_guidance: Use firewall rules to limit internal access
Monitor remote service activity and authentication events

evidence.description: Heartbleed is a vulnerability in affected versions of OpenSSL that can allow an attacker to read sensitive information from process memory through a malicious TLS heartbeat request.
indicators: Unexpected TLS heartbeat requests
Abnormally large heartbeat payload requests
TLS heartbeat requests containing inconsistent payload length
Unexpected responses containing sensitive memory contents
Network activity targeting vulnerable TLS services
Connections to systems running vulnerable OpenSSL versions
detection_guidance: Identify systems and services using affected OpenSSL versions
Monitor TLS heartbeat traffic for anomalous request patterns
Inspect unusual heartbeat request and response sizes
Review network traffic involving potentially vulnerable TLS services
Correlate suspicious TLS activity with system and application logs
Check whether vulnerable OpenSSL versions have been patched
mitigation_guidance: Upgrade OpenSSL to a fixed version
Restart affected services after remediation where required
Revoke and replace potentially exposed credentials
Regenerate and replace potentially compromised TLS certificates
Monitor affected systems for follow-on compromise
